subject: business-studies
title: Break-Even: Where Revenue Catches Total Cost

questions.prompt: A business has fixed costs of $2,000, variable cost of $10 per unit and a selling price of $20 per unit. What is its break-even output?

choices.text: 100 units, because $2,000 divided by $20 selling price is 100
Total cost starts at zero, so break-even cannot be read from fixed costs
200 units, because $2,000 fixed costs divided by $10 contribution per unit is 200
400 units, because fixed costs must be covered twice

questions.misconception: Fixed costs rise as output rises, so total cost starts at zero like revenue.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Fixed costs rise as output rises, so total cost starts at zero like revenue. In fact Fixed costs stay flat at $2,000 at every output, so total cost starts at the fixed-cost intercept and rises only by the $10 variable cost per unit; total revenue starts at zero and rises faster at the $20 selling price, so the two lines cross once, at the break-even output of 200 units. Contribution is $20 minus $10, which is $10 per unit, so $2,000 divided by $10 gives the break-even output of 200 units.

questions.prompt: At zero output, what is total cost for this business?

choices.text: $2,000, because fixed costs must still be paid even at zero output
$10, because one unit of variable cost is counted
$4,000, because that is the break-even revenue

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: total cost starts at the fixed-cost intercept, so at zero output total cost is the $2,000 of fixed costs, before any variable cost is added.

questions.prompt: A student says total cost starts at zero like revenue. Explain, in two sentences, where each line actually starts and why.
questions.answer: Fixed costs stay flat at $2,000 at every output, so total cost starts at the fixed-cost intercept and rises only by the $10 variable cost per unit; total revenue starts at zero and rises faster at the $20 selling price, so the two lines cross once, at the break-even output of 200 units.
questions.explanation: The deciding habit is to check each starting point: fixed costs are flat, total cost starts at fixed costs, and only revenue and variable cost start at zero.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state total revenue and total cost at the break-even point.
questions.answer: At break-even output of 200 units, total revenue and total cost are both $4,000, so there is neither profit nor loss.
questions.explanation: Scene 4 shows the two lines crossing once at 200 units, where both values are $4,000.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the break-even chart stages in order?

choices.text: Flat fixed-cost line at $2,000, total cost rises from $2,000, revenue rises faster from zero, lines cross at 200 units
Revenue rises from zero, flat fixed-cost line, lines cross, total cost rises from zero
Total cost rises from zero, revenue rises, flat fixed-cost line, lines cross at 200 units
Lines cross at 200 units, total cost rises, revenue rises, flat fixed-cost line

questions.explanation: Scene 1 draws the flat fixed-cost line, scene 2 adds total cost from the $2,000 intercept, scene 3 adds faster-rising revenue, and scene 4 marks the crossing at 200 units.
